Container.Name: Filehub
Container.Overview: Filehub is a lightweight, self-hosted file manager for sharing folders among users on your own server.
Container.Description:
Filehub is a lightweight, self-hosted file manager for sharing folders among users on your own server.
Features include per-user home folders, shared folders with read/write access and an optional Allow delete flag, sharing a file or folder with other Filehub users or a public link, WebDAV at /dav/, folder and resumable (chunked) uploads, a 100 GiB default upload cap, SMTP notices, image/PDF/video previews, ffmpeg thumbnails, and optional TOTP 2FA.
First boot: leave ADMIN_PASSWORD unset. After the container starts, open /mnt/user/appdata/nas-filehub/admin-credentials.txt for the generated admin password, sign in, then change it under Settings → Change password. That credentials file is written once and is never overwritten.
Prefer a reverse proxy with HTTPS, and set SECURE_COOKIES=true and PUBLIC_BASE_URL once you are behind HTTPS. If the proxy is not on loopback, set TRUSTED_PROXIES. Set HSTS on the reverse proxy (Filehub does not enable it). Do not expose the WebUI port directly to the public internet.
Optional hardware thumbnails: keep the /dev/dri device mapping (and NVIDIA runtime if you use an NVIDIA GPU) and set THUMB_HWACCEL=auto (or leave THUMB_VAAPI=true for the same auto path). If no GPU device is present, leave hardware acceleration off. The image supports linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Set PUID/PGID to the host UID/GID that should own /data (default 1000:1000).
Appdata is mounted at /data (database, thumbnails, and admin-credentials.txt). Optionally map User files from /mnt/user/nas-filehub to /data/files (DATA_ROOT) so user data is stored on a share instead of under appdata. If the container has already been started, move any existing files from appdata/nas-filehub/files into the new User files location before adding that mapping, otherwise the new mount hides the old directory. The optional Unraid shares path is mounted at /data/files/shares so you can create shared folders with paths such as shares/Movies. If you also set User files, keep Unraid shares mapped when you still want host /mnt/user visible as shares/…; otherwise you can remove it.
Container.Requires: After the first start, read the generated admin password in /mnt/user/appdata/nas-filehub/admin-credentials.txt, then change it under Settings → Change password. Prefer a reverse proxy; do not expose the WebUI port to the public internet. For hardware thumbnails, keep /dev/dri mapped (or an NVIDIA runtime) and set THUMB_HWACCEL=auto, or THUMB_VAAPI=true for the same auto path. If no GPU device is present, remove the device mapping. PUID/PGID default to 1000:1000.
Container.Changes: Filehub v0.4.14 template and GHCR image. Features include share with users or a public link, WebDAV, folder and resumable uploads, a 100 GiB default upload cap, and an optional User files mapping. Leave ADMIN_PASSWORD unset on first boot and read the generated password from appdata/nas-filehub/admin-credentials.txt.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTP WebUI port (container 8080). Prefer a reverse proxy; do not expose this port directly to the public internet.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, thumbnails, and generated admin-credentials.txt. User files default to /data/files inside this folder unless User files is mapped separately.

Config.Name: User files
Config.Description: Optional DATA_ROOT mapping for homes and shared folders you create in Filehub. Default host path is /mnt/user/nas-filehub. If the container already ran, move appdata/nas-filehub/files here before adding this mapping. PUID/PGID ownership applies to /data, including this mount.

Config.Name: Unraid shares
Config.Description: Optional mapping so Shared folders can use paths like shares/Movies from the Unraid /mnt/user tree. You can remove this mapping if you do not need host shares. If User files is also set, keep this mapping only when you still want host shares visible under shares/.

Config.Name: Intel GPU (/dev/dri)
Config.Description: Optional GPU devices for thumbnail acceleration (Intel/AMD VAAPI via /dev/dri). If not present on the host, remove this mapping and leave THUMB_HWACCEL empty / THUMB_VAAPI=false.

Config.Name: ADMIN_USER
Config.Description: Seed admin username on first boot only.

Config.Name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Optional. Leave empty on first boot so the entrypoint generates a password into /data/admin-credentials.txt. Only seeds the first boot; later changes must be made in Settings.

Config.Name: SECURE_COOKIES
Config.Description: Set true when the WebUI is served over HTTPS (reverse proxy). Leave false so http://IP:port login works on a first Unraid install.

Config.Name: THUMB_ENABLE
Config.Description: Generate image and video thumbnails with ffmpeg.

Config.Name: THUMB_VAAPI
Config.Description: Legacy flag. true enables auto hardware thumbnail acceleration (same as THUMB_HWACCEL=auto). Honored when THUMB_HWACCEL is unset.

Config.Name: THUMB_HWACCEL
Config.Description: auto, off, vaapi, or nvdec. Empty defers to THUMB_VAAPI. ffmpeg always falls back to software on failure.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: UID the container uses after start, and the owner of /data. Default 1000 matches previous images.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: GID the container uses after start, and the group owner of /data. Default 1000.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Optional umask for created files (for example 002). Leave empty to use the default.

Config.Name: PUBLIC_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Public site URL used in password-reset emails (for example https://filehub.example.com). Required for public HTTPS deployments, together with SECURE_COOKIES=true.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_PROXIES
Config.Description: Optional comma-separated IPs or CIDRs of reverse proxies allowed to set X-Forwarded-For. Loopback is always trusted. Set this if the proxy is not on localhost.

Config.Name: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT
Config.Description: Max login and share-link unlock attempts per client IP per minute. Authenticated WebDAV requests are not counted.

Config.Name: LOGIN_LOCKOUT_LIMIT
Config.Description: Failed logins per username before a temporary account lock.

Config.Name: LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES
Config.Description: Account lock duration in minutes. Further attempts during the lock do not extend the window.

Config.Name: MAX_UPLOAD_MB
Config.Description: Maximum upload size in MiB (application default is 102400, or 100 GiB). Set 0 to disable the application cap; user and storage quotas still apply.
